rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes varying Al content across alloys, whereas the paper anneals a single fixed-composition alloy at different temperatures. This is a different kind of intervention (composition change vs. heat treatment).
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis mentions high-temperature tensile tests at 600 °C, ion irradiation, cryogenic Charpy tests, and corrosion tests, while the paper uses annealing at 1100–1300 °C followed by water quenching and room-temperature hardness testing. These are different testing regimes.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes lattice distortion and Al-driven ordering to form B2 in an FCC matrix, while the paper describes spinodal decomposition of BCC into Ni–Al-lean and Ni–Al-rich regions, followed by ordering to B2, with reciprocal BCC/B2 nanostructures. These are different mechanisms.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts improved high-temperature strength, radiation tolerance, environmental resistance, and cryogenic toughness with B2 formation, whereas the paper predicts and measures increased room-temperature hardness with higher annealing temperature. The predicted properties and direction differ.
